newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Sugar-China sugar prices up, tolling hard.
newsitem.headline: Asian Sugar-China sugar prices up, tolling hard.

text.p: China's domestic sugar prices have started climbing as the summer sets in and consumption increases, trade sources said on Wednesday.

Sugar traders said the price of white sugar in the southern producing province of Guangxi had inched up to between 4,000 yuan (US$482) and 4,100 yuan (US$494) per tonne from last week's range of 3,950 yuan to 4,000 yuan per tonne.
Many mills were offering white sugar at above 4,000 yuan per tonne but most transactions were concluded at a shade under 4,000 yuan, one China-based source said.

Large sugar companies in east and central China had started stocking up in preparation for summer demand, some sources said, noting this was a departure from the earlier philosophy of buying on a hand-to-mouth basis.

There was still tolling demand, but traders in Hong Kong and China said end-users were looking for prompt shipments in June or July and were unwilling to pay high prices for forward shipments in August.
Thai shippers said last week that China was expected to speed up tolling -- importing raw sugar for processing and re-export -- with rising white-to-raw premiums.

If China imported raw sugar from Thailand for tolling now, cargoes would arrive at port by June and the processed sugar readied for export in August, just when buyers were scarce, China and Hong Kong traders said.
"The premium is wider than before, but the key problem is what end-users will pay for Chinese sugar," said one trader.
Chinese white sugar to Pakistan, for example, was around US$380 per tonne, C&F Karachi, the China source said.
"White premium over raws is around $74. On this basis, if we do tolling, we still make a small loss," a senior Chinese trader said.
Buying and selling sugar at fixed prices meant breaking even or making a profit was very difficult, he said.

"If we buy on a premium basis against No. 11 and sell on another premium basis against No. 5, maybe you can take a chance on the futures markets and earn some money, but sometimes you can lose a great deal of money," the trader said.
Thai raw sugar premiums for May/July delivery were quoted at 0.60/0.63 cents a pound (bid/offer) over New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) futures on a FOB basis.
July/September deliveries were quoted at 0.55/0.65 cents.
Local traders said there was still concern in the market over whether U.S. trade house Cargill would find buyers for Brazilian and Central American raw sugar.
"We're watching if the Cargill operation is affecting the London white sugar prices," another trader said.
Last week, some traders in Hong Kong cited talk that Cargill was pushing up the London white sugar price for Russian refineries.
China produced 6.604 million tonnes of sugar in the 1996/97 crushing season (October-April), up 376,000 tonnes from the last season, an official said.
China imported 130,000 tonnes of sugar in the first four months of 1997, down 41.8 percent from the same period in 1996.
Imports in April were 80,000 tonnes while exports were 27,423 tonnes.
-- Mishi Saran in Hong Kong (852) 2843 6358
-- Eiichiro Tokumoto in Tokyo (813) 3432 7391
